title: In vitro expansion of Wilms’ tumor protein 1 epitope-specific primary T cells
author: van der Heijden, Flumens, et al.
materials: Isotype control panel AIgG2b1 μLIgG2b1 μLIgG11 μLPanel BFITCVolumePEVolumePE-Cy7VolumeTube

steps.title: Prepare HLA‑A2/WT137‑45 tetramers
steps.instruction: Thaw MHC monomers on ice, add streptavidin‑APC at a 4:1 monomer:streptavidin ratio by adding one‑fifth of the total streptavidin‑APC, mix 20 min on ice in the dark using a shaker, repeat the addition and mixing four times, then store tetramers protected from light at 4 °C for up to 2 months.

steps.title: Determine donor HLA‑A2 status
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL whole blood to a non‑sterile FACS tube, add 100 µL mouse anti‑human HLA‑A2 primary antibody and incubate 15 min at 20‑22 °C, add 4 mL RBC lysis buffer and incubate 10 min at room temperature, centrifuge 480 × g 5 min (20‑22 °C) and decant supernatant, add 1 µL FITC‑conjugated rabbit anti‑mouse secondary antibody and incubate 10 min at room temperature in the dark, add 2 mL FACS buffer, wash by centrifuging 480 × g 5 min (20‑22 °C) and discard buffer, resuspend in 100 µL FACS buffer and analyse by flow cytometry; include a secondary‑only negative control. If staining PBMCs, omit the lysis step and wash after the primary antibody with 2 mL FACS buffer.

steps.title: Isolate CD14+ monocytes from fresh PBMCs
steps.instruction: Count PBMCs (max 1.0 × 10⁹ total, max 1.0 × 10⁸ per LS column), wash with MACS buffer and centrifuge 480 × g 5 min (20‑22 °C), add 8 µL MACS buffer per 1 × 10⁶ PBMCs, add 2 µL CD14 microbeads per 1 × 10⁶ PBMCs, mix and incubate 15 min at 2‑8 °C, dilute with MACS buffer to a total volume of 50 mL (≈10× initial volume), centrifuge 480 × g 5 min and decant, resuspend pellet in 5 µL MACS buffer per 1 × 10⁶ cells, place LS columns in a magnetic separator, rinse each column with 3 mL MACS buffer (wait until buffer passes completely), apply the cell suspension, collect the CD14‑ flow‑through in a 50 mL Falcon tube, wash the column three times with 3 mL MACS buffer (add new buffer only after the previous volume has passed, avoid bubbles), remove the column, add 5 mL MACS buffer onto the column outside the magnetic field and flush out the magnetically labeled CD14+ cells by firmly pushing the plunger, add MACS buffer up to 10 mL to the CD14+ cell tube, count CD14+ and CD14‑ fractions and assess viability (automatic counter or PI staining). If CD8+ T cells will be isolated the same day, add MACS buffer up to 50 mL to the CD14‑ tube; if isolation is postponed, resuspend CD14‑ cells in 30 mL AIM‑V medium and place on a roller overnight (15‑18 h). Centrifuge CD14+ cells 480 × g 5 min, discard buffer, and resuspend monocytes in DC culture medium at a seeding density of ≥1.3 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Assess monocyte purity by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Take two aliquots of 0.1 × 10⁶ CD14+ cells, stain one with 1 µL IgG2b‑FITC isotype control and the other with 1 µL CD14‑FITC, incubate 15 min at 20‑22 °C in the dark, wash once with 2 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge 480 × g 5 min (20‑22 °C) and discard supernatant, resuspend in 100 µL FACS buffer and analyse by flow cytometry; expect >95 % CD14+ among live cells and ≥90 % viability.

steps.title: Phenotype mature IL‑4 dendritic cells
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.4 × 10⁶ harvested DCs to a non‑sterile FACS tube, centrifuge 480 × g 5 min (20‑22 °C) and discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 400 µL FACS buffer, block with 4 µL mouse γ‑globulin (1 µL per 100 µL) for 10 min at room temperature (no wash), aliquot 0.1 × 10⁶ blocked cells per tube for staining with panels A and B (see Table 1), incubate 15 min at room temperature in the dark, wash with 2 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge 480 × g 5 min (20‑22 °C) and discard buffer, add 50 µL 7‑AAD solution (2 µL 7‑AAD + 50 µL FACS buffer) per sample, incubate 10 min at room temperature, then acquire data on a flow cytometer.

steps.title: Determine CD8+ T‑cell frequency in PBL fraction
steps.instruction: Transfer 0.1 × 10⁶ cells to a non‑sterile FACS tube, add 5 µL CD3‑PE, 5 µL CD4‑PerCP and 5 µL CD8‑FITC, incubate 15 min at room temperature in the dark, wash once with 2 mL FACS buffer, centrifuge 480 × g 5 min and discard supernatant, resuspend in 100 µL FACS buffer and analyse by flow cytometry to calculate the percentage of CD3⁺CD8⁺ T cells for subsequent magnetic labeling.

steps.title: Isolate CD8+ T cells by magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Label the PBL fraction with CD8 magnetic microbeads according to the manufacturer’s instructions, run the suspension through LS columns in a magnetic separator, collect the CD8+ fraction, then assess purity and viability using the same staining protocol as in the monocyte purity step (isotype control and CD8‑FITC staining).

steps.title: Cryopreserve CD8+ T cells and CD8‑ fraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 480 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, resuspend cells at 1.0 × 10⁷ cells per 1.5 mL cold freezing medium, aliquot 1.5 mL per cryovial, place vials in a −80 °C freezing container (e.g., Mr. Frosty) for 4‑12 h, then transfer to liquid nitrogen; work quickly after adding DMSO‑containing freezing medium to limit exposure at room temperature.

description: This protocol describes the specific steps for in vitro expansion of WT1 epitope-specific primary CD8+ T cells from healthy donor PBMCs. By means of human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-A∗02:01 (hereafter termed as HLA-A2)/WT1 tetramer staining, expanded specific T cells can be analyzed to assess WT1 epitope-specific T-cell reactivity, sequenced for TCR repertoire, or (single-cell) sorted to generate T-cell clones for the discovery of epitope-specific TCR sequences for the development of TCR-engineered cell therapies. Purified CD8+ T cells are expanded in two rounds of in vitro stimulation (IVS). For the first IVS of 8 days, autologous dendritic cells (DCs) are used, which are differentiated from freshly isolated CD14+ monocytes and after maturation pulsed with immunodominant HLA-A2-restricted WT137-45 epitope. After priming of the naïve CD8+ T cells, irradiated autologous peptide-pulsed CD14- and CD8- depleted peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBLs) are used for the second IVS of 8 days. Expanded WT1-specific T cells are detected with fluorochrome-labeled WT1-specific tetramers, allowing quantification and sorting of epitope-specific T cells, for further downstream applications. The preparatory steps above describe the isolation and generation of mature IL-4 DCs and CD8+ T cells from fresh PBMCs. The following sections describe the further use of these cells. The positively selected CD8+ T cells are cryopreserved upon isolation, to be then thawed and specifically activated (on day 1) and expanded in two rounds of IVS; first (on day 1) with fresh or thawed autologous mDCs, second with thawed irradiated autologous PBL, originating from the CD14- and CD8- cell fractions that are cryopreserved to be used upon irradiation for second IVS (on day 8 after 1st IVS).
